Music machines

Musical pinball

v′ = v−2(v·n)n
f = f₀·2^(s/12)

Mechanism and sound mapping

A seeded ball reflects off five bumpers and the table walls. Collision time triggers the note and its visual flash; bumper identity chooses a pentatonic degree and a short bell reply. Ball speed controls the boing brightness. Launch angle changes the actual trajectory. Wall hits are softer bass taps. Scan progress is t=0…1; machine events occupy t≤0.88 and the closing answer t=0.9…0.952. Each event has a smooth attack, an exponential body and a release. Pitch is an equal-tempered pentatonic degree over root 146.8324 Hz. The simulation and score are fixed by the seed, including control settings after ~. Vivid plays the event instruments; Original uses the legacy pitch-curve voice.

Puzzle-piece harmony

connected pieces → interlocking phrases
pieceᵢ → voiceᵢ

Mechanism and sound mapping

Six matching pieces assemble into a two-row picture. Each connection activates another interlocking musical part; the default replay assembles the remaining pieces automatically. Drag a piece onto its matching numbered home, or use Connect next. Initial connections are saved in the seed. Scan progress is t=0…1; machine events occupy t≤0.88 and the closing answer t=0.9…0.952. Replay and interaction

Press Play sound to animate and hear the same event timeline. Change a control to recalculate the sequence. Magnet dragging pauses the scan and applies the new field on release. Puzzle pieces snap only to their own numbered homes; connections activate more interlocking parts. Position sliders and Connect next provide keyboard alternatives.

Each machine uses a seeded pentatonic scale and dedicated wood, bell, bass, boing, click or whistle tones. The closing three-note answer starts after the simulation. Settings are encoded after ~ in the seed and included in the URL. Identical seed, sound mode and scan duration reproduce the same timeline. All 133 earlier patterns remain available.
